title: Grateful Dead Live at Albuquerque Civic Auditorium on 1971-11-17

ai_review.summary: Despite a sub‑par microphone‑captured FM broadcast (mono mix, occasional boom and splices), the show bursts with high energy, highlighted by a smoking "The Other One" and a memorable Ramble On Rose encore.
ai_review.review: This recording preserves an exuberant late‑1971 performance where Jerry rides a three‑hour marathon, Keith’s piano shines, and the band locks into fierce jams, especially on The Other One. Technically the source is a mic‑recorded FM broadcast with mono mix, boomy bass and tape splices that limit fidelity, but the musical fire more than compensates for those flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.0 stars; most praise the show’s energy and jams while repeatedly noting recording shortcomings, leading to a strong overall impression but tempered by technical issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Microphone capture of an FM broadcast; mono mix with occasional boomy bass, hiss and tape splices; some sections break off after a splice; overall listenable but below professional soundboard standards.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Energetic throughout with a high‑octane first set and a jam‑heavy second set; the band stays tightly locked, delivering powerful transitions especially into The Other One.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as on a roll for three hours, animated, bluegrass‑style picking, and generally delivering high energy throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted as particularly active in jams, pushing riffs during The Other One and maintaining strong interplay with the rest of the band.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano praised for beautiful playing and instantly adapting to drive the jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy (Bill) described as an animal throughout the performance.
